why: Components that grow as cells arrive: re-running a flood fill after every addition is too slow, but union-find handles it online. A new land cell adds one island, and every union with a neighbouring land cell in a different set removes one.
hints: When one water cell turns to land, which islands can it affect?
Only its up to four land neighbours. Count +1 for the new cell, then union it with each land neighbour; every union that actually merges two sets is -1.
Index cells as r * cols + c, keep a land flag, union-find with path compression and union by size. Re-adding existing land appends the unchanged count. O(k alpha(rows * cols)).
pitfalls: A repeated position must not add another island.
Two neighbours may already share a root; only decrement when find differs.
